info.title: galata-tower
info.description: A read API over the galata-datawatch record. It watches the record, not the worker.

200.description: The archive root and the tape's prune columns

get.summary: Closed days still holding more segments than compaction should have left.
get.description:
`max_segments` is the caller's threshold, because what counts as too many is
an operator's judgement and this reports rather than judges.

get.summary: Every venue's status, as it arrives.
get.description:
SSE rather than a WebSocket: the traffic is one-directional, and the
browser's `EventSource` reconnects, backs off and honours `retry:` without a
line of client code.

200.description: A server-sent event stream of venue status snapshots

get.summary: One dataset, over a window, as the durable bound permits.
get.description:
**Decimals arrive as strings.** See `tape.rs`: serialising with
`arrow-json` would send them unquoted, and `JSON.parse` would round every
price before anything could decline to.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: quotes, trades, candles, funding or marks

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most rows to return. Defaults to `tape::DEFAULT_LIMIT`.

200.description: The window's rows, and the durable bound

400.description: An unknown dataset, or a window that runs backwards

About.description:
What this tower reads, and how the tape may be narrowed.

The screen builds its own queries, and `prune_on` is what makes a windowed
read cheap — so it is served rather than duplicated in TypeScript, where it
would be a second copy free to disagree.

prune_on.description: The tape columns a reader can prune on, from the schema itself.

Overdue.description:
A closed day still holding more segments than compaction should have left.

**Reported, never judged.** The number is here; whether it is bad belongs to
whoever set the threshold.

segments.description: How many segments it still holds.

Partition.description: One partition of the record, as the store lists it.

path.description: Its path relative to the archive root.

Snapshot.description:
One venue's status, exactly as it was published.

The payload is not parsed here. The tower forwards what the venue said; the
screen's types come from the contract, and a tower that re-typed the
snapshot would be a second statement of it free to disagree.

subject.description: The subject it arrived on, e.g. `status.hyperliquid`.

venue.description: The venue, taken from the subject.

View.description: A window's rows, and how far the store is durable.

bound.description:
How far the store has durably written, in the tape's own sequence.

**Returned with the rows on purpose.** Forty rows from a quiet hour and
forty rows from a store that stopped there look identical without it.

rows.description:
The rows, each a map of column to value. Decimals are strings.

When a cap applies these are the NEWEST in the window — a reader
watching a tape wants its end — and `total` is what makes that
truncation visible rather than inferred.

total.description:
How many rows the window holds, before any cap.

**Always present, not only when a cap applied.** A field that appears
conditionally is one callers learn to ignore, and this is the only thing
distinguishing a capped read from a quiet window.
